zh: 每一轮的起点是当前最左的非零元素 x，而这一轮结束后起点自身一定变成 0（它减去了自己），起点左边本来就全是 0。所以下一轮的起点只会出现在更右边，不需要每次从头找。
一轮的扫描从起点开始向右，只要当前元素 ≥ x 就减去 x 继续；一旦遇到严格小于 x 的元素（包括 0）就立刻结束本轮，不能跳过它继续。每一轮都把固定的 x 累加进结果。
从左到右枚举位置 i：若 a[i] 为 0 就跳过；否则令 x = a[i]，结果加 x，然后从 j = i 起，当 a[j] ≥ x 时执行 a[j] −= x 并 j++，遇到更小的值就停。n ≤ 100，O(n²) 足够；结果不超过所有元素之和 ≤ 10^8。
en: Each round starts at the current leftmost nonzero element x, and after the round that starting element itself is 0 (it subtracted itself), while everything to its left was already 0. So the next start can only be further right, and you never need to search from the beginning.

A round scans rightwards from the start: while the current element is at least x, subtract x and continue; as soon as an element strictly smaller than x appears (including 0), the round ends immediately, without skipping over it. Every round adds the fixed x to the result.

Go through positions i from left to right: skip a[i] if it is 0; otherwise let x = a[i], add x to the result, and starting from j = i, do a[j] -= x and j++ while a[j] >= x, stopping at the first smaller value. With n <= 100, O(n^2) is plenty, and the result never exceeds the sum of the elements, at most 10^8.

explanationEn:
## Fixed original OCR and correction of the curated page

The source is OA LIST/eBay_OA/027_image.txt through 031_image.txt at the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc. Image 027 states explicitly: find the current leftmost nonzero element x and try to subtract x moving right from its position; if an element strictly smaller than x is met, go immediately to step 3 (add x), rather than skipping that element and continuing to the right. Equal values can be subtracted. Image 031 gives the complete ranges 1<=n<=100 and 0<=numbers[i]<=1000000, with an all-zero array allowed; the output is the integer accumulated in step 3.

The company MDX misstates "move on to step3" as skip, and the attached code in three languages also continues scanning, which made the original examples look contradictory. This site follows the formal rules of the consecutive OCR images, the complete execution trace, and the bounds, and only corrects the rules on the curated page without changing the original example answers; no upstream code was executed. The standard input uses a two-line serialization of n and n numbers.

Original example 1 is [3,3,5,2,3]. The first round subtracts 3 only from the first three items and stops immediately at 2, giving [0,0,2,2,3], not [0,0,2,2,0]; the second round subtracts 2 starting at the third item, giving [0,0,0,0,1]; the third round subtracts 1, for a total of 6. Original example 2 is [5,5,5,5]; one round subtracts 5 from everything, and the answer is 5. The third public example, [4,0,4], is added by this site: the 0 in the middle is strictly smaller than 4 and blocks the first round, so 4 is added twice and the result is 8. The two original examples keep their original inputs and outputs.

## Approach

Keep a copy of the array and check positions i from left to right. If the value is 0, skip it; otherwise record x=a[i], add it to the result, and subtract x item by item from the longest contiguous range starting at i whose values are all at least x. Stop this round as soon as the first value smaller than x is met.

There is no need to search for the nonzero element from the beginning in every round: the starting element of each round becomes exactly 0, and earlier positions always stay 0, so the next round can continue from the following position. Note that a 0 inside the range must not be skipped; like any other value smaller than x, it blocks this round's scan.

## Proof of correctness

Before the outer loop handles position i, all positions smaller than i are 0. If a[i]=0, skipping it cannot miss a starting point of the original algorithm. If a[i]>0, it is exactly the leftmost nonzero element the original algorithm requires. The inner loop keeps x fixed and subtracts only while the current element is at least x, stopping as soon as a smaller element is met, so the range it modifies is exactly the same as in the original step 2. Each round adds x exactly once, which is also the same as step 3.

After the subtraction, position i becomes 0 and all elements further left stay 0, so the loop invariant continues to hold. Each position becomes a nonzero starting point at most once, so there are at most n rounds, and in the end every position is 0. By induction, the state and the running result after each round agree with the original algorithm, so the output is correct.

## Complexity and full range

At most n rounds, each scanning at most n items to the right: O(n^2) time and O(n) space for the copy. With n<=100 there are about ten thousand inner checks at most, and there is no need to subtract 1 at a time by value. In each round x reduces the starting element by at least x, and array elements only decrease, so the running result does not exceed the initial sum of elements, <=100000000, and a 32-bit signed integer is enough. An all-zero input runs no rounds and returns 0; the value 1000000 and equal values are handled directly.

## Independent validation

The oracle for the 163 unique small inputs uses immutable array states: find the first nonzero item, enumerate all contiguous prefixes starting there whose items are all at least x, take the longest one, build a whole new tuple, and recurse. It does not call the reference program and does not reuse the in-place scan; it computes the accumulated value directly from the original state transitions. In addition, all 5460 inputs of length 1..6 with values 0..3 were enumerated exhaustively, comparing the original reference function with the independent state oracle, and the validated input domain and a summary were saved; this part is an in-process enumeration, while the 163 oracle inputs and all formal cases were additionally run as real subprocesses.

The formal data include the two original examples, this site's zero-blocking example, all zeros, zeros at the start and end, strictly increasing/decreasing arrays, repeated thresholds, alternating 0 and 1000000, full random 100-item arrays, and multi-level remainders. Large boundary cases use the independent state oracle and are additionally checked against easy closed forms, for example 100 equal maximum values add only 1000000, and 50 maximum values separated by 0 give 50000000. The two wrong programs follow the MDX skip and the incorrect use of <= as the blocking condition, respectively; both must exit normally and actually print wrong answers.
